passages.text: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions left the believers.
They felt torn as they departed from them.
They sailed straight to Cos.
The next day, they sailed to Rhodes.
From Rhodes, they traveled to Patara.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπ’ αὐτῶν εὐθυδρομήσαντες ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν Κῶ τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Πάταρα

passages.text: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
passages.sermon: We found a ship going to Phoenicia.\r\nWe boarded the ship.\r\nWe set sail.
passages.original: καὶ εὑρόντες πλοῖον διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην ἐπιβάντες ἀνήχθημεν

passages.text: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions traveled by ship.
They saw the island of Cyprus.
They passed to the south of Cyprus.
They continued sailing toward Syria.
They arrived at the city of Tyre in Syria.
The ship stopped at Tyre to unload its cargo.
passages.original: ἀναφάναντες δὲ τὴν Κύπρον καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον ἐπλέομεν εἰς Συρίαν καὶ κατήλθομεν εἰς Τύρον ἐκεῖσε γὰρ τὸ πλοῖον ἦν ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον

passages.text: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions arrived in Tyre.
They looked for the disciples there.
They found the disciples.
Paul and his companions stayed with the disciples for seven days.
The disciples spoke to Paul.
The Holy Spirit guided the disciples.
The disciples told Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Ἀνευρόντες δὲ τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐπεμείναμεν αὐτοῦ ἡμέρας ἑπτά οἵτινες τῷ Παύλῳ ἔλεγον διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος μὴ ἐπιβαίνειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions stayed in Tyre for seven days.
Their time in Tyre ended.
Paul and his companions prepared to leave.
All the disciples in Tyre came with them.
The disciples brought their wives and children.
They all walked together out of the city.
They reached the beach.
Everyone knelt down on the sand.
They prayed together on the beach.
passages.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐξαρτίσαι ἡμᾶς τὰς ἡμέρας ἐξελθόντες ἐπορευόμεθα προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων σὺν γυναιξὶ καὶ τέκνοις ἕως ἔξω τῆς πόλεως καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν προσευξάμενοι

passages.text: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.
passages.sermon: We said goodbye to each other.\r\nWe went aboard the ship.\r\nThe disciples and their families returned to their own homes.
passages.original: ἀπησπασάμεθα ἀλλήλους καὶ ἐνέβημεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὰ ἴδια

passages.text: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.
passages.sermon:
We finished our voyage from Tyre.
We arrived at Ptolemais.
We greeted the brothers there.
We stayed with them for one day.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸν πλοῦν διανύσαντες ἀπὸ Τύρου κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἐμείναμεν ἡμέραν μίαν παρ’ αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.
passages.sermon:
We left the next day.
We traveled to Caesarea.
We entered the house of Philip.
Philip was an evangelist.
Philip was one of the Seven chosen men.
We stayed with Philip.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντες ἤλθομεν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φιλίππου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐμείναμεν παρ’ αὐτῷ

passages.text: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
passages.sermon:
Philip was an evangelist.
Philip was one of the Seven.
Philip had four daughters.
All four daughters were unmarried.
All four daughters were virgins.
All four daughters prophesied.
passages.original: τούτῳ δὲ ἦσαν θυγατέρες τέσσαρες παρθένοι προφητεύουσαι

passages.text: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
passages.sermon: We stayed in Caesarea for several days.\r\nA prophet came from Judea.\r\nHis name was Agabus.
passages.original: Ἐπιμενόντων δὲ ἡμέρας πλείους κατῆλθέν τις ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας προφήτης ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος

passages.text: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’ ”
passages.sermon:
A prophet named Agabus came to us from Judea.
He took Paul’s belt.
He tied his own feet and hands with the belt.
He spoke to us.
He said, “The Holy Spirit says this.”
He said, “The man who owns this belt will be tied up like this in Jerusalem.”
He said, “The Jews in Jerusalem will bind him.”
He said, “They will hand him over to the Gentiles.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου δήσας ἑαυτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν Τάδε λέγει τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον Τὸν ἄνδρα οὗ ἐστιν ἡ ζώνη αὕτη οὕτως δήσουσιν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν

passages.text: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
We heard the prophet’s message.
The prophet Agabus warned us about Paul’s future in Jerusalem.
We understood that Paul would face danger there.
We pleaded with Paul.
The local people also pleaded with Paul.
We all begged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ ἠκούσαμεν ταῦτα παρεκαλοῦμεν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἐντόπιοι τοῦ μὴ ἀναβαίνειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul spoke to the people who were with him.
Paul saw that they were weeping.
Paul saw that they were breaking his heart.
Paul asked them, "Why are you weeping?"
Paul asked them, "Why are you breaking my heart?"
Paul said he was ready to be bound in Jerusalem.
Paul said he was also ready to die in Jerusalem.
Paul said he would do this for the name of the Lord Jesus.
passages.original: Τότε ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Παῦλος Τί ποιεῖτε κλαίοντες καὶ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐ μόνον δεθῆναι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀποθανεῖν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἑτοίμως ἔχω ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: When he would not be dissuaded, we fell silent and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”
passages.sermon:
Paul refused to change his mind.
We stopped trying to persuade him.
We became quiet.
We said, “The Lord’s will be done.”
passages.original: μὴ πειθομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡσυχάσαμεν εἰπόντες Τοῦ Κυρίου τὸ θέλημα γινέσθω

passages.text: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: We finished these days.\r\nWe prepared our things.\r\nWe traveled to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας ἐπισκευασάμενοι ἀνεβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple.
passages.sermon:
Some disciples lived in Caesarea.
These disciples traveled with us.
They brought us to a man named Mnason.
Mnason was from Cyprus.
Mnason was an early disciple.
We stayed at Mnason’s house.
passages.original: συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν ἀπὸ Καισαρείας σὺν ἡμῖν ἄγοντες παρ’ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν Μνάσωνί τινι Κυπρίῳ ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ

passages.text: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.
passages.sermon:
We arrived in Jerusalem.
The brothers were there.
They welcomed us.
They welcomed us with joy.
passages.original: Γενομένων δὲ ἡμῶν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀσμένως ἀπεδέξαντο ἡμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοί

passages.text: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian leader and apostle.
James was a leader in the Jerusalem church.
The elders were leaders in the church.
The next day came.
Paul went with us to see James.
All the elders were present.
passages.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰσῄει ὁ Παῦλος σὺν ἡμῖν πρὸς Ἰάκωβον πάντες τε παρεγένοντο οἱ πρεσβύτεροι

passages.text: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
passages.sermon:
Paul greeted the elders and James.
Paul spoke to them.
Paul told them what God had done.
God had worked among the Gentiles.
God did these things through Paul’s ministry.
Paul explained each thing God had done, one by one.
passages.original: καὶ ἀσπασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐξηγεῖτο καθ’ ἓν ἕκαστον ὧν ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the elders and to James.
Paul told them what God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
The elders and James listened to Paul.
They glorified God.
They spoke to Paul.
They said, “Brother, look at the Jews who have believed.
There are many thousands of them.
All of these Jewish believers are zealous for the law.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεόν εἶπόν τε αὐτῷ Θεωρεῖς ἀδελφέ πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσὶν ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τῶν πεπιστευκότων καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τοῦ νόμου ὑπάρχουσιν

passages.text: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.
passages.sermon:
Many Jews have heard reports about you, Paul.
They believe you teach Jews who live among the Gentiles.
They think you tell these Jews to turn away from Moses.
They think you tell them not to circumcise their children.
They think you tell them not to follow our customs.
passages.original: κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάντας Ἰουδαίους λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσιν περιπατεῖν

passages.text: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.
passages.sermon:
Paul had arrived in Jerusalem.
\r\nMany Jewish believers were present.
\r\nThese Jews were zealous for the law.
\r\nSome people believed Paul taught Jews to abandon Moses.
\r\nThey thought Paul told Jews not to circumcise their children.
\r\nThey also thought Paul told Jews not to follow Jewish customs.
\r\nThe leaders spoke to Paul.
\r\nThey said, “What should we do?”
\r\nThey said, “The people will certainly hear that you have come.”
passages.original: τί οὖν ἐστιν πάντως ἀκούσονται ὅτι ἐλήλυθας

passages.text: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.
passages.sermon:
We are speaking to you, Paul, a Jewish Christian leader.
Some people believe you teach Jews to abandon the law of Moses.
We want to address this concern.
We give you this advice.
There are four men with us.
These men have taken a vow.
passages.original: Τοῦτο οὖν ποίησον ὅ σοι λέγομεν εἰσὶν ἡμῖν ἄνδρες τέσσαρες εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ἐφ’ ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.
passages.sermon:
Paul, you are a follower of Jesus and a Jew.
Take these four men who have made a vow.
Join them in their purification ceremony.
Purify yourself together with them.
Pay the expenses for these men.
This will allow them to shave their heads.
Everyone will see what you do.
Everyone will know the truth about you.
They will see that the rumors about you are false.
They will know you also live in obedience to the law.
passages.original: τούτους παραλαβὼν ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς ἵνα ξυρήσονται τὴν κεφαλήν καὶ γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ὧν κατήχηνται περὶ σοῦ οὐδέν ἐστιν ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖς καὶ αὐτὸς φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον

passages.text: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”
passages.sermon:
Gentile believers are people from non-Jewish nations who have faith in Jesus.
We have written instructions to these Gentile believers.
We decided that they must avoid certain things.
They must not eat food offered to idols.
They must not eat blood.
They must not eat meat from animals that were strangled.
They must not practice sexual immorality.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἐθνῶν ἡμεῖς ἐπεστείλαμεν κρίναντες φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς τό τε εἰδωλόθυτον καὶ αἷμα καὶ πνικτὸν καὶ πορνείαν

passages.text: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul took the men with him.
The next day, Paul purified himself with these men.
Paul and the men went into the temple together.
Paul announced the time when their purification would be finished.
Paul said that an offering would be made for each man.
passages.original: Τότε ὁ Παῦλος παραλαβὼν τοὺς ἄνδρας τῇ ἐχομένῃ ἡμέρᾳ σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς εἰσῄει εἰς τὸ ἱερόν διαγγέλλων τὴν ἐκπλήρωσιν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ ἁγνισμοῦ ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου αὐτῶν ἡ προσφορά

passages.text: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him, crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”
passages.sermon:
Some Jews came from the province of Asia.
They saw Paul in the temple.
The Jews from Asia stirred up the whole crowd.
They seized Paul.
They shouted loudly.
They said, “Men of Israel, help us!”
They accused Paul.
They said, “This is the man who teaches everywhere against our people.”
They said, “He teaches against our law.”
They said, “He teaches against this place.”
They said, “He has brought Greeks into the temple.”
They said, “He has defiled this holy place.”
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι θεασάμενοι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ συνέχεον πάντα τὸν ὄχλον καὶ ἐπέβαλον ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας κράζοντες Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται βοηθεῖτε οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ κατὰ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τοῦ τόπου τούτου πάντας πανταχῇ διδάσκων ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ κεκοίνωκεν τὸν ἅγιον τόπον τοῦτον

passages.text: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
passages.sermon: Some Jews from Asia had seen Trophimus with Paul in the city.\r\nTrophimus was from Ephesus.\r\nThese Jews thought Paul had brought Trophimus into the temple.
passages.original: ἦσαν γὰρ προεωρακότες Τρόφιμον τὸν Ἐφέσιον ἐν τῇ πόλει σὺν αὐτῷ ὃν ἐνόμιζον ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν εἰσήγαγεν ὁ Παῦλος

passages.text: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.
passages.sermon:
The people in Jerusalem heard a commotion.
The whole city became excited.
A large crowd gathered quickly.
The people seized Paul.
They dragged Paul out of the temple.
Immediately, someone shut the temple gates.
passages.original: Ἐκινήθη τε ἡ πόλις ὅλη καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενοι τοῦ Παύλου εἷλκον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι

passages.text: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.
passages.sermon:
Paul was in danger.
People were trying to kill Paul.
A commander led a Roman regiment in Jerusalem.
Someone reported to the commander.
The report said that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.
passages.original: Ζητούντων τε αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀνέβη φάσις τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης ὅτι ὅλη συνχύννεται Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
passages.sermon:
The Roman commander heard that the city was in turmoil.
He acted immediately.
He took some soldiers and centurions with him.
He ran down to the crowd.
The people saw the commander and the soldiers.
They stopped beating Paul.
passages.original: ὃς ἐξαυτῆς παραλαβὼν στρατιώτας καὶ ἑκατοντάρχας κατέδραμεν ἐπ’ αὐτούς οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας ἐπαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον

passages.text: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
passages.sermon:
The Roman commander approached Paul.
The commander arrested Paul.
The commander ordered the soldiers to bind Paul with two chains.
The commander asked Paul who he was.
The commander asked Paul what he had done.
passages.original: Τότε ἐγγίσας ὁ χιλίαρχος ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκέλευσεν δεθῆναι ἁλύσεσι δυσί καὶ ἐπυνθάνετο τίς εἴη καὶ τί ἐστιν πεποιηκώς

passages.text: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.
passages.sermon:
The crowd was confused.
Some people shouted one thing.
Other people shouted something else.
The commander was present.
He could not learn the truth.
The noise was too great.
The commander gave an order.
He ordered the soldiers to bring Paul into the barracks.
passages.original: Ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι ἐπεφώνουν ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ μὴ δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸν θόρυβον ἐκέλευσεν ἄγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν

passages.text: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle.
The soldiers arrested Paul.
The mob acted violently.
Paul reached the steps.
The soldiers carried Paul.
They carried him because the mob was violent.
passages.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀναβαθμούς συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ τὴν βίαν τοῦ ὄχλου

passages.text: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!”
passages.sermon: A large crowd followed Paul.\r\nThe people in the crowd shouted loudly.\r\nThey shouted, “Away with him!”
passages.original: ἠκολούθει γὰρ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ κράζοντες Αἶρε αὐτόν

passages.text: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?” “Do you speak Greek?” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia.
Soldiers were about to take Paul into the barracks.
Paul spoke to the commander.
Paul asked, “May I say something to you?”
The commander replied, “Do you speak Greek?”
passages.original: Μέλλων τε εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τῷ χιλιάρχῳ Εἰ ἔξεστίν μοι εἰπεῖν τι πρὸς σέ Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ἑλληνιστὶ γινώσκεις

passages.text: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the ‘Assassins’ into the wilderness?”
passages.sermon:
The Roman commander spoke to Paul.
He asked Paul a question.
He said, “Aren’t you the Egyptian?”
He referred to an Egyptian man who caused trouble some time ago.
This Egyptian led a rebellion.
He took four thousand men with him.
These men were called the ‘Assassins.’
He led them into the wilderness.
passages.original: οὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος ὁ πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστατώσας καὶ ἐξαγαγὼν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους ἄνδρας τῶν Σικαρίων

passages.text: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the commander.
Paul said, “I am a Jew.”
I am from Tarsus in Cilicia.
Tarsus is an important city.
I am a citizen of Tarsus.
I ask you for permission.
Please let me speak to the people.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος Ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος μέν εἰμι Ἰουδαῖος Ταρσεὺς τῆς Κιλικίας οὐκ ἀσήμου πόλεως πολίτης δέομαι δέ σου ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν

passages.text: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:
passages.sermon:
Paul received permission to speak.
Paul stood on the steps.
Paul motioned to the crowd with his hand.
The crowd became very quiet.
Paul spoke to the people in Hebrew.
passages.original: ἐπιτρέψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν κατέσεισεν τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης προσεφώνησεν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ λέγων
